es.why_it_matters: Examinar cómo los modelos abiertos impulsan la comprensión y simulación del entorno físico ayuda a entender el rumbo de la robótica y los sistemas autónomos.
es.extended_analysis:
A medida que la IA trasciende la nube para integrarse en la realidad física, se requieren metodologías innovadoras de inferencia y simulación. El episodio explora la visión de NVIDIA sobre estas tecnologías emergentes.

Asimismo, se debate la importancia de la apertura en los modelos para fomentar la innovación y los requisitos técnicos para desarrollar sistemas de IA física altamente funcionales.
es.context: La convergencia entre la inteligencia artificial y el hardware físico impulsa el desarrollo de nuevos enfoques en simulación y modelado para aplicaciones robóticas y de vehículos autónomos.
key_takeaways: La importancia de los modelos abiertos para fomentar la innovación colaborativa.
El papel de los modelos de mundos en la simulación del entorno físico.
Perspectivas sobre la construcción de sistemas de inteligencia artificial física.
highlights: Invitado: Ming-Yu Liu, vicepresidente de Cosmos Lab en NVIDIA.
Presentadores: Daniel Whitenack y Chris Benson.

zh-CN.title: 开放模型与NVIDIA物理AI的未来
zh-CN.summary: Daniel和Chris邀请NVIDIA Cosmos Lab副总裁Ming-Yu Liu做客节目，探讨人工智能向机器人、车辆等物理系统延伸的趋势。他们共同讨论了开放模型、世界模型以及仿真技术的最新进展。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 了解开放模型与世界模型如何帮助AI理解并模拟物理世界，对于把握机器人与自动驾驶技术的未来至关重要。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
随着人工智能从云端走向现实世界的物理系统，推理、仿真和模型构建的方法正在发生深刻变化。本期节目探讨了NVIDIA在物理AI领域的视角与规划。

讨论同时聚焦于开放模型对推动技术创新的重要意义，以及构建功能日益强大的物理AI系统所面临的关键考量。
zh-CN.context: 人工智能正加速向机器人学和智能交通等物理领域渗透，这促使业界寻找更加强大的仿真框架和世界模型来应对现实环境的复杂性。

de.title: Offene Modelle und die Zukunft der Physical AI mit NVIDIA
de.summary: Daniel und Chris sprechen mit Ming-Yu Liu, Vice President des Cosmos Lab bei NVIDIA, über den Übergang der KI in physische Systeme wie Roboter und Fahrzeuge. Sie beleuchten die Rolle offener Modelle, World Models und neuartiger Simulationsansätze.
de.why_it_matters: Zu verstehen, wie offene Modelle und Simulationen KI-Systeme befähigen, die physische Welt zu begreifen, ist entscheidend für die nächste Welle robotischer Innovationen.
de.extended_analysis:
Während Künstliche Intelligenz zunehmend den Sprung aus der Cloud in physische Geräte vollzieht, entstehen neue Anforderungen an Inferenz und Modellierung. Die Episode beleuchtet NVIDIAs Perspektive auf diese technologischen Entwicklungen.

Dabei wird erörtert, warum Offenheit für die Innovationskraft unerlässlich ist und welche Voraussetzungen für die Konstruktion leistungsfähiger physischer KI-Systeme erfüllt sein müssen.
de.context: Die Verschmelzung von KI mit Robotik und autonomen Fahrzeugen erfordert fortschrittliche Simulationsumgebungen und präzise World Models, um reale Umgebungen adäquat abbilden zu können.
key_takeaways: Die Bedeutung offener Modelle für kollaborative technologische Fortschritte.
Wie World Models die Simulation und das Verständnis der physischen Welt unterstützen.
Einblicke in die Entwicklung leistungsfähiger Physical-AI-Infrastrukturen.
highlights: Gast: Ming-Yu Liu, Vice President von Cosmos Lab bei NVIDIA.
Moderatoren: Daniel Whitenack und Chris Benson.

items.title: From Math Olympiads to Navier-Stokes: How Fast Is AI Progressing? with Greg Burnham - #778
items.summary: AI systems have gone from struggling with grade-school math to helping solve research problems that have resisted mathematicians for decades, including Navier-Stokes. In this episode, Greg Burnham, who leads AI capabilities research at Epoch AI, joins us to examine what that progress says about where AI is going. We look at how these systems are solving hard math problems, how much they rely on persistence and prior human work, and whether they are starting to produce genuinely new ideas. We also discuss how to measure progress as traditional benchmarks become less useful, why capability gains appear surprisingly steady across model generations, and where models still struggle with open-ended work, learning from experience, and identifying promising new research directions. 🗒️ Full show notes: https://twimlai.com/go/778.
items.podcastDescription: Ricerca, machine learning e applicazioni raccontati da ricercatori e professionisti.

it.title: Dalle Olimpiadi di Matematica a Navier-Stokes: i progressi dell'IA
it.summary: Analizziamo l'evoluzione dei sistemi di intelligenza artificiale, passati da compiti scolastici a problemi di ricerca complessi come le equazioni di Navier-Stokes. Ne discute Greg Burnham di Epoch AI nel podcast di TWIML.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere il ritmo reale dei progressi dell'IA e i suoi limiti attuali è fondamentale man mano che i vecchi parametri di riferimento perdono efficacia.
it.extended_analysis:
In questo episodio del TWIML AI Podcast, l'ospite Greg Burnham, responsabile della ricerca sulle capacità di IA presso Epoch AI, esamina i progressi dei modelli intelligenti. La discussione affronta come tali sistemi affrontano problemi matematici avanzati, il loro livello di dipendenza dal lavoro umano precedente e dalla persistenza, e se stiano iniziando a generare idee genuinamente nuove.

Vengono inoltre analizzati i metodi per misurare i progressi quando i benchmark tradizionali diventano obsoleti, la stabilità dei guadagni di capacità tra le diverse generazioni di modelli e le sfide ancora aperte in aree come il lavoro aperto e l'apprendimento dall'esperienza.
it.context: Il panorama dell'intelligenza artificiale evolve rapidamente, sollevando interrogativi su come misurare in modo affidabile le capacità dei modelli di fronte a problemi di ricerca matematica e scientifica di frontiera.
key_takeaways: I sistemi IA passano da test scolastici a problemi complessi come Navier-Stokes.
Greg Burnham analizza come misurare i progressi quando i vecchi benchmark perdono utilità.
Vengono esaminati i limiti attuali nell'apprendimento dall'esperienza e nella ricerca aperta.
highlights: Ospite: Greg Burnham, Epoch AI.
Argomenti: Olimpiadi di matematica, equazioni di Navier-Stokes e misurazione dei progressi.

en.title: From Math Olympiads to Navier-Stokes: How Fast Is AI Progressing?
en.summary: We explore how AI systems have advanced from grade-school math to tackling complex research problems like Navier-Stokes. Greg Burnham of Epoch AI joins the TWIML AI Podcast to examine what this means for future progress.
en.why_it_matters: As traditional benchmarks become less useful, accurately measuring capability gains and understanding model limits is critical for charting the future of AI.
en.extended_analysis:
In episode 778 of The TWIML AI Podcast, host discussions focus on how modern AI systems solve hard math problems, their reliance on persistence and prior human work, and whether they are beginning to produce genuinely new ideas. Guest Greg Burnham, who leads AI capabilities research at Epoch AI, shares insights on how to measure progress when standard metrics fall short.

The conversation also covers why capability gains appear surprisingly steady across model generations, alongside the persistent challenges models face with open-ended work, learning from experience, and identifying promising research directions.
en.context: As AI models advance into advanced scientific domains, researchers face the challenge of updating evaluation frameworks to accurately gauge true progress versus reliance on prior human data.
key_takeaways: AI systems are moving from basic math to tackling long-standing mathematical research problems.
Traditional evaluation benchmarks are losing their effectiveness, necessitating new ways to measure progress.
Models still face notable hurdles in open-ended tasks and learning directly from experience.
highlights: Guest: Greg Burnham, lead of AI capabilities research at Epoch AI.
Key topics: Math Olympiads, Navier-Stokes, and steady generational capability gains.

es.title: De las Olimpiadas de Matemáticas a Navier-Stokes: el avance de la IA
es.summary: Analizamos cómo los sistemas de IA han evolucionado desde problemas escolares hasta resolver cuestiones complejas como Navier-Stokes. Greg Burnham, de Epoch AI, examina este progreso en el podcast de TWIML.
es.why_it_matters: A medida que los benchmarks tradicionales pierden utilidad, comprender la velocidad real y los límites del desarrollo de la IA resulta esencial.
es.extended_analysis:
En este episodio del podcast TWIML AI, el experto Greg Burnham aborda el ritmo del progreso de la inteligencia artificial. La charla explora cómo los modelos abordan problemas matemáticos avanzados, su dependencia del trabajo humano previo y si están comenzando a generar ideas verdaderamente originales.

Asimismo, se discuten los métodos para medir avances ante la obsolescencia de los indicadores clásicos, la constancia en las mejoras generacionales y los obstáculos pendientes en tareas abiertas y aprendizaje autónomo.
es.context: El rápido desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial exige nuevas metodologías de evaluación para medir con precisión las capacidades reales de los modelos en la investigación científica.
key_takeaways: La IA pasa de resolver matemáticas escolares a abordar problemas de investigación complejos.
Se examina cómo medir el progreso cuando los benchmarks tradicionales ya no son suficientes.
Se analizan las dificultades actuales de los modelos en tareas abiertas y aprendizaje por experiencia.
highlights: Invitado: Greg Burnham, investigador principal de capacidades de IA en Epoch AI.
Temas clave: Olimpiadas matemáticas, Navier-Stokes y evolución generacional.

zh-CN.title: 从数学奥赛到纳维-斯托克斯：人工智能进展有多快？
zh-CN.summary: 我们探讨人工智能系统如何从处理基础数学题，发展到协助解决困扰数学家数十年的纳维-斯托克斯等研究难题。Epoch AI的格雷格·伯纳姆做客TWIML AI播客深入解析。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 随着传统基准测试逐渐失去效用，准确衡量模型能力并理解其局限性对于把握人工智能的未来至关重要。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
在本期TWIML AI播客中，主讲嘉宾、Epoch AI人工智能能力研究负责人格雷格·伯纳姆（Greg Burnham）探讨了AI系统如何解决高难度数学问题、它们对先前人类工作和持续性的依赖程度，以及它们是否开始产生真正的新创意。

讨论还涵盖了在传统基准不再适用时如何衡量进展、跨模型代际的能力提升为何表现得异常稳定，以及模型在开放式任务、从经验中学习和识别研究方向方面仍面临哪些挑战。
zh-CN.context: 随着人工智能模型向高级科学领域挺进，研究人员正面临如何更新评估框架、以准确衡量真实进展的挑战。
key_takeaways: 人工智能系统正从基础数学转向攻克长期未决的数学研究难题。
传统评估基准正在失效，亟需探索测量进展的新方法。
模型在开放式任务和直接从经验中学习方面仍面临显著障碍。
highlights: 嘉宾：Epoch AI人工智能能力研究负责人格雷格·伯纳姆（Greg Burnham）。
核心议题：数学奥林匹克、纳维-斯托克斯方程及代际能力提升。

de.title: Von Mathe-Olympiaden zu Navier-Stokes: Wie schnell schreitet KI voran?
de.summary: Wir beleuchten, wie KI-Systeme von einfachen Schulaufgaben zu komplexen Forschungsproblemen wie Navier-Stokes fortgeschritten sind. Greg Burnham von Epoch AI analysiert diesen Trend im TWIML AI Podcast.
de.why_it_matters: Da traditionelle Benchmarks an Nutzen verlieren, ist es entscheidend, Leistungssteigerungen und Modellgrenzen präzise zu verstehen, um die Zukunft der KI einzuschätzen.
de.extended_analysis:
In dieser Episode des TWIML AI Podcasts diskutiert Greg Burnham, Leiter der KI-Fähigkeitenforschung bei Epoch AI, den aktuellen Stand und die Geschwindigkeit der KI-Entwicklung. Die Unterhaltung beleuchtet, wie moderne Modelle schwierige mathematische Probleme lösen, inwieweit sie auf menschliche Vorarbeiten angewiesen sind und ob sie erste originäre Ideen hervorbringen.

Zudem wird erörtert, wie Fortschritte gemessen werden können, wenn Standard-Benchmarks veraltet sind, warum Leistungszuwächse über Generationen hinweg konstant wirken und wo Modelle bei offenen Aufgaben und dem Lernen aus Erfahrung nach wie vor Schwierigkeiten haben.
de.context: Mit dem Vordringen von KI in anspruchsvolle wissenschaftliche Domänen stehen Forschende vor der Herausforderung, verlässliche Bewertungsmethoden für echte Fortschritte zu finden.
key_takeaways: KI-Systeme bewältigen zunehmend komplexe mathematische Forschungsprobleme.
Traditionelle Leistungsmetriken verlieren an Relevanz, was neue Messmethoden erfordert.
Modelle stoßen bei offenen Aufgaben und dem Erfahrungslernen weiterhin auf Hürden.
highlights: Gast: Greg Burnham, Leiter der KI-Fähigkeitenforschung bei Epoch AI.
Themen: Mathe-Olympiaden, Navier-Stokes-Gleichungen und stetiger Generationsfortschritt.

it.title: Da AGENTS.md al deployment aziendale
it.summary: Gli agenti IA stanno passando dai prototipi ai sistemi aziendali, dove sicurezza, conformità e affidabilità sono essenziali. Nick Kuhn di VMware Tanzu Platform discute con i conduttori di cosa cambia nell'integrazione di questi strumenti insieme alle applicazioni tradizionali.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere il passaggio dei prototipi IA agli ambienti di produzione aziendali offre chiarezza su sicurezza, conformità e scalabilità.
it.extended_analysis:
Mentre l'adozione dell'intelligenza artificiale cresce, le organizzazioni affrontano sfide inedite legate alla distribuzione e alla gestione operativa. In questo episodio, l'analisi si concentra sulle lezioni apprese dall'ingegneria delle piattaforme tradizionale e sul loro adattamento ai carichi di lavoro basati su agenti.

Vengono approfonditi aspetti critici come i gateway MCP, la memoria condivisa, l'identità e la protezione in sandbox, offrendo una panoramica concreta per i team software che pianificano l'adozione di queste tecnologie nelle proprie infrastrutture.
it.context: L'episodio esamina il punto di contatto tra le nuove tecnologie di intelligenza artificiale e i requisiti rigidi dei sistemi IT aziendali consolidati.
key_takeaways: Gli agenti IA richiedono ora standard di sicurezza e conformità pari alle applicazioni tradizionali.
L'esperienza dell'ingegneria delle piattaforme offre modelli utili per la gestione dei nuovi agenti.
Gestione dell'identità e sandboxing sono cruciali nei deployment aziendali.
highlights: Nick Kuhn di VMware Tanzu Platform partecipa come ospite principale.
La discussione copre argomenti come agent build packs, gateway MCP e memoria condivisa.

en.title: From AGENTS.md to Enterprise Deployment
en.summary: AI agents are moving beyond laptops and prototypes into enterprise environments where security, compliance, and reliability matter. Nick Kuhn from VMware Tanzu Platform joins the hosts to discuss what changes when deploying agents alongside traditional applications.
en.why_it_matters: As enterprises adopt AI agents, understanding how to handle security, scalability, and integration with traditional infrastructure becomes critical for software teams.
en.extended_analysis:
Moving AI agents from local development environments to production grade systems presents significant architectural and security challenges. This episode explores the intersection of modern AI workflows and established platform engineering practices.

Discussions cover practical components such as agent build packs, Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateways, shared memory, identity management, and sandboxing, providing a comprehensive look at what organizations must consider today.
en.context: The discussion bridges the gap between experimental artificial intelligence development and the strict requirements of enterprise IT operations.
key_takeaways: Enterprise deployment demands rigorous security, compliance, and scalability for AI agents.
Platform engineering principles offer valuable lessons for managing modern agent architectures.
Key technical components include MCP gateways, shared memory, and sandboxing mechanisms.
highlights: Nick Kuhn from VMware Tanzu Platform joins Daniel Whitenack and Chris Benson.
Practical advice is shared for organizations adopting agents in production environments.

es.title: De AGENTS.md al despliegue empresarial
es.summary: Los agentes de IA dejan atrás los prototipos para entrar en entornos empresariales donde la seguridad y la fiabilidad son clave. Nick Kuhn de VMware Tanzu Platform analiza los cambios al implementar agentes junto a aplicaciones tradicionales.
es.why_it_matters: A medida que las empresas adoptan agentes de IA, comprender la seguridad y la escalabilidad resulta fundamental para los equipos de desarrollo.
es.extended_analysis:
El salto de los agentes de inteligencia artificial desde los entornos de desarrollo locales hasta la producción plantea importantes retos arquitectónicos. Este episodio examina cómo las prácticas tradicionales de ingeniería de plataformas se adaptan a los flujos de trabajo de la IA.

Se abordan componentes prácticos como los paquetes de compilación de agentes, las pasarelas MCP, la memoria compartida y el aislamiento en entornos seguros, ofreciendo una visión completa para las organizaciones.
es.context: El episodio conecta el desarrollo experimental de la inteligencia artificial con los rigurosos requisitos operativos de la tecnología empresarial.

it.summary: In questo episodio, Daniel e Chris esplorano con Liam Dunne e Ben Moore di Discovered Labs la transizione dalla SEO tradizionale alla ricerca basata sull'intelligenza artificiale, analizzando il funzionamento dei modelli linguistici.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere le dinamiche della ricerca IA è fondamentale per adattarsi a un ecosistema in cui i modelli generano risposte dirette e interagiscono per conto degli utenti.
it.extended_analysis: La ricerca basata sull'intelligenza artificiale sta ridefinendo il modo in cui le persone e i brand affrontano la visibilità online. Durante l'episodio, gli ospiti approfondiscono concetti chiave come la strategia su Reddit, il meccanismo di query fan-out, la rappresentazione nei pesi dei modelli e il consenso, offrendo uno sguardo dietro le quinte su ciò che accade quando un LLM genera una risposta. Vengono inoltre esaminate le implicazioni future di un web in cui gli agenti IA non si limitano a scoprire i siti, ma compiono azioni per gli utenti.
it.context: Il passaggio dai motori di ricerca tradizionali ai sistemi di intelligenza artificiale genera nuove sfide per la visibilità digitale e la gestione dei contenuti online.

Analisi di concetti come query fan-out, consenso e rappresentazione nei modelli.
Prospettive future sugli agenti IA che interagiscono direttamente con i siti web.

items.title: From Voice Agents to AI Avatars with Alexander Smola - #777
items.summary: Voice AI has gotten remarkably good, but natural conversation remains a high bar. Small delays, awkward interruptions, or the wrong tone can quickly break the illusion—and adding vision and visual presence only raises the stakes. In this episode, Alex Smola, co-founder and CEO of Boson AI, explores the path from today’s voice agents to audiovisual agents and AI avatars. We discuss the technical tradeoffs behind real-time voice, including audio tokenization, latency, model size, and inference cost, as well as what changes when these systems can both see and be seen. We also explore the role of emotional intelligence in AI, how agents can learn from human interactions, and what it will take to move beyond impressive demos toward interactions that actually feel natural. 🗒️ Full show notes: https://twimlai.com/go/777.

it.title: Dagli assistenti vocali agli avatar IA con Alexander Smola
it.summary: In questo episodio, il co-fondatore e CEO di Boson AI Alexander Smola analizza il passaggio dagli attuali agenti vocali agli agenti audiovisivi e agli avatar IA. Vengono esaminati i compromessi tecnici legati alla voce in tempo reale, tra cui latenza, tokenizzazione audio e costi d'inferenza.
it.why_it_matters: Migliorare la naturalezza della conversazione e aggiungere una presenza visiva rappresenta una sfida cruciale per superare la fase delle semplici dimostrazioni e rendere le interazioni davvero efficaci.
it.extended_analysis:
La conversazione naturale tramite intelligenza artificiale incontra ancora ostacoli legati a ritardi, interruzioni impreviste e tonalità inadeguate. L'introduzione della visione e della presenza visiva aumenta ulteriormente la complessità tecnica.

Nel corso dell'episodio vengono affrontati i compromessi tecnici della voce in tempo reale, analizzando aspetti come l'audio tokenization, la latenza, le dimensioni dei modelli e i costi di inferenza. Si discute inoltre del ruolo dell'intelligenza emotiva e della capacità degli agenti di apprendere dalle interazioni umane.
it.context: Il podcast esplora l'evoluzione tecnologica dei sistemi di intelligenza artificiale conversazionale, esaminando il passaggio dai modelli vocali tradizionali alle nuove frontiere degli avatar visivi e audiovisivi.
key_takeaways: I compromessi tecnici del parlato in tempo reale includono latenza e tokenizzazione.
L'aggiunta della componente visiva e degli avatar accresce la complessità progettuale.
L'intelligenza emotiva e l'apprendimento dalle interazioni umane sono centrali per la naturalezza.
highlights: Ospite dell'episodio è Alexander Smola, co-fondatore e CEO di Boson AI.
Vengono analizzati i costi di inferenza e le dimensioni dei modelli per gli agenti vocali.

Natural conversation with AI remains difficult due to small delays, awkward interruptions, and tone management, while adding visual presence raises the stakes even further.

en.context: The episode investigates the technical and design challenges involved in evolving conversational AI systems from simple voice agents into fully realized audiovisual avatars.
key_takeaways: Real-time voice involves managing latency, model size, and audio tokenization.
Visual integration and avatars significantly increase system complexity.
Emotional intelligence and human feedback are key to natural communication.

es.title: De agentes de voz a avatares de IA con Alexander Smola

es.why_it_matters: Superar las limitaciones actuales en la naturalidad de la conversación y añadir una presencia visual es fundamental para ir más allá de las demostraciones y lograr interacciones reales.

La conversación natural con inteligencia artificial aún enfrenta desafíos como retrasos y tonos incorrectos, y la incorporación de la visión eleva la complejidad técnica.

El episodio aborda las compensaciones técnicas detrás de la voz en tiempo real, incluyendo la tokenización de audio, la latencia, el tamaño del modelo y los costos de inferencia. También se explora el papel de la inteligencia emotiva y el aprendizaje a través de interacciones humanas.

La inteligencia emocional es fundamental para mejorar la naturalidad de las respuestas.

zh-CN.title: 从语音智能体到AI虚拟形象：对话亚历山大·斯莫拉

zh-CN.why_it_matters: 实现自然的对话并加入视觉存在感，是超越单纯的精彩演示、迈向真正流畅互动必须克服的关键门槛。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
由于细微的延迟、尴尬的中断或不当的语调，与人工智能进行自然对话依然存在挑战，而引入视觉感知则进一步增加了系统的复杂性。

节目深入探讨了实时语音的技术权衡，涉及音频分词、延迟、模型规模和推理成本。同时，讨论还涉足了人工智能中情感智能的作用，以及智能体如何从人类互动中进行学习。
zh-CN.context: 本期节目聚焦于对话式人工智能的技术演进，探讨将传统语音代理升级为具备视觉能力的综合化虚拟形象所面临的工程挑战。
key_takeaways: 实时语音技术需要权衡延迟、模型大小与音频分词。
视觉集成的引入显著提升了系统的设计难度。
情感智能与人机交互学习是实现自然对话的核心要素。

de.context: Der Podcast beleuchtet die technologische Entwicklung von konversationalen KI-Systemen hin zu multimodalen audiovisuellen Avataren.
key_takeaways: Echtzeit-Sprachsysteme erfordern die Handhabung von Latenz und Tokenisierung.
Visuelle Avatare erhöhen die technische Komplexität und die Designanforderungen.
Emotionale Intelligenz ist wichtig für natürlich wirkende Mensch-KI-Interaktionen.
highlights: Zu Gast ist Alexander Smola, Mitbegründer und CEO von Boson AI.
Thematisiert werden die technischen Herausforderungen von Sprachagenten und KI-Avataren.

items.title: Do AI Tokenomics Matter More Than Model Benchmarks? with Chris Potts - #776
items.summary: As reasoning models consume more tokens and AI systems become more expensive to run, understanding what those tokens actually buy is becoming increasingly important. In this episode, Stanford professor and Big Spin co-founder Chris Potts joins us to discuss AI tokenomics and his research into “tokenflation”—the possibility that token usage is growing faster than the measurable value those tokens produce. We explore how to measure the return on AI spending, why benchmarks alone provide an incomplete picture of model progress, and what inference-time scaling means for the economics of increasingly capable models. Chris also explains why expert AI users tend to get better results by challenging and iterating with models, how AI fluency affects outcomes, and why more efficient architectures could change the underlying economics. We also discuss DSPy, interpretability, the limits of today’s transformer architectures, and where Chris sees opportunities for more fundamental innovation in AI. 🗒️ Full show notes: ⁠⁠https://twimlai.com/go/776.
items.podcastDescription: Ricerca, machine learning e applicazioni raccontati da ricercatori e professionisti.

it.title: L'economia dei token nell'era dell'intelligenza artificiale
it.summary: In questo episodio, Chris Potts di Stanford esplora il concetto di tokenflation e il ritorno sull'investimento dei modelli di IA. Esaminiamo perché i benchmark tradizionali offrono un quadro incompleto e come l'efficienza economica stia diventando cruciale.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere i costi di calcolo e l'efficienza dei token è essenziale ora che i modelli di ragionamento consumano più risorse ed è necessario misurare il reale valore prodotto.
it.extended_analysis:
Man mano che i sistemi di intelligenza artificiale diventano più costosi da eseguire, l'attenzione si sposta dai semplici benchmark alle cosiddette tokenomics. Chris Potts discute il fenomeno della tokenflation, analizzando se l'uso dei token stia crescendo più rapidamente del valore generato.

L'episodio approfondisce l'impatto dello scaling in fase di inferenza e il ruolo dell'esperienza utente, mostrando come la capacità di interagire e sfidare i modelli migliori i risultati. Vengono inoltre toccati argomenti come DSPy, l'interpretabilità e i limiti delle attuali architetture transformer.

Il dibattito si apre infine sulle opportunità di innovazione fondamentale nell'IA, esaminando architetture più efficienti in grado di ridefinire i costi operativi e la sostenibilità economica a lungo termine.
it.context: L'evoluzione dei modelli di intelligenza artificiale spinge l'industria a interrogarsi non solo sulle prestazioni pure, ma anche sulla sostenibilità economica e sulla scalabilità dei costi di calcolo.
key_takeaways: La crescita dell'uso dei token solleva interrogativi sul valore reale prodotto dai modelli.
I benchmark tradizionali non sono più sufficienti per valutare i progressi complessivi dell'IA.
L'efficienza delle architetture e la fluency degli utenti giocano un ruolo chiave nei risultati.
highlights: Ospite Chris Potts, professore di Stanford e co-fondatore di Big Spin.
Discussione approfondita su tokenflation e tokenomics dell'IA.

en.title: Do AI Tokenomics Matter More Than Model Benchmarks?
en.summary: Stanford professor Chris Potts joins the podcast to discuss AI tokenomics and the concept of tokenflation. The episode examines how to measure the return on AI spending beyond traditional benchmarks.
en.why_it_matters: As reasoning models consume more tokens and running AI systems becomes costlier, understanding the actual value delivered by these tokens is increasingly vital for sustainable development.
en.extended_analysis:
With AI systems growing more expensive to operate, evaluating model progress requires looking past standard benchmarks and examining the economics of token consumption. Chris Potts explores tokenflation, investigating whether token usage is outpacing the measurable value produced by these systems.

The conversation covers inference-time scaling, the importance of AI fluency, and how expert users achieve better results through iterative challenges. It also addresses technical themes such as DSPy, interpretability, and transformer limits.

Finally, the discussion highlights potential areas for fundamental innovation, considering how more efficient architectures might reshape the underlying economics of advanced AI models.
en.context: The rapid adoption of reasoning-heavy AI models has brought operational costs and economic efficiency to the forefront of industry discussions.
key_takeaways: Tokenflation highlights the risk of token usage growing faster than measurable value.
Benchmarks alone offer an incomplete picture of overall model progress.
Expert user interaction styles significantly impact the outcomes achieved with AI.
highlights: Featuring Stanford professor and Big Spin co-founder Chris Potts.
Exploration of inference-time scaling and AI token economics.

es.title: ¿Importan más la tokenomía de la IA que los benchmarks?
es.summary: El profesor de Stanford Chris Potts analiza la tokenomía de la IA y el fenómeno de la tokenflation. El episodio explora cómo medir el retorno de la inversión más allá de los benchmarks tradicionales.
es.why_it_matters: A medida que los modelos de razonamiento consumen más recursos, comprender el valor real que aportan los tokens se vuelve fundamental para la sostenibilidad económica de la IA.
es.extended_analysis:
Con el aumento de los costos operativos de los sistemas de inteligencia artificial, evaluar el progreso tecnológico exige mirar más allá de las pruebas tradicionales. Chris Potts analiza la llamada tokenflation para determinar si el uso de tokens está creciendo más rápido que el valor real que producen.

El episodio también aborda el escalado en tiempo de inferencia, la importancia de la fluidez en el uso de la IA y cómo los usuarios expertos obtienen mejores resultados mediante la iteración. Asimismo, se discuten temas como DSPy, la interpretabilidad y los límites de los transformers.

Por último, se señalan oportunidades para una innovación más fundamental en arquitecturas eficientes que puedan transformar la economía subyacente de estos modelos.
es.context: El enfoque de la industria se está desplazando hacia la eficiencia económica ante el incremento en los costos de ejecución de los modelos de lenguaje avanzados.
key_takeaways: La tokenflation cuestiona si el volumen de tokens se traduce en un valor proporcional.
Los benchmarks actuales resultan insuficientes para medir el progreso completo del modelo.
La experiencia del usuario influye de forma directa en la calidad de los resultados obtenidos.
highlights: Con la participación de Chris Potts, profesor de Stanford y cofundador de Big Spin.
Análisis detallado de la economía de los tokens y el escalado en inferencia.

zh-CN.title: AI代币经济学是否比模型基准测试更重要？
zh-CN.summary: 斯坦福大学教授Chris Potts做客节目，探讨AI代币经济学与“代币通胀”现象。本期节目探讨了如何衡量AI支出的回报，以及为什么基准测试无法完全反映模型进展。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 随着推理模型消耗更多代币且运行成本不断上升，理解这些代币带来的实际价值对于评估AI系统的可持续性至关重要。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
随着人工智能系统的运行成本不断攀升，行业关注点逐渐从单一的性能基准转向代币经济学。Chris Potts探讨了“代币通胀”的概念，即代币使用量的增长是否超过了其所产生的可衡量价值。

节目深入探讨了推理时扩展、AI熟练度对结果的影响，以及专家用户如何通过持续的交互获得更好的输出。此外，讨论还涉及了DSPy、可解释性以及当前Transformer架构的局限性。

最后，访谈展望了更基础的创新机会，探讨高效架构如何改变高级人工智能模型的底层经济逻辑。
zh-CN.context: 随着资源密集型推理模型的普及，运营成本和经济效益已成为人工智能领域的核心议题。
key_takeaways: 代币通胀揭示了代币消耗增长可能快于实际价值产出的风险。
单纯的基准测试无法全面展现模型的整体进步情况。
用户对AI的熟练运用和交互方式对最终结果产生显著影响。
highlights: 嘉宾为斯坦福大学教授、Big Spin联合创始人Chris Potts。
探讨了推理时扩展与AI代币经济学的核心议题。

de.title: Sind AI-Tokenomics wichtiger als klassische Benchmarks?
de.summary: Stanford-Professor Chris Potts diskutiert über AI-Tokenomics und das Phänomen der Tokenflation. Die Episode beleuchtet, wie sich der tatsächliche Nutzen von Tokens jenseits klassischer Benchmarks messen lässt.
de.why_it_matters: Da immer mehr ressourcenintensive Modelle zum Einsatz kommen, wird ein tieferes Verständnis der ökonomischen und tatsächlichen Werte hinter dem Token-Verbrauch entscheidend.
de.extended_analysis:
Mit steigenden Betriebskosten für fortschrittliche KI-Systeme reicht der Blick auf reine Leistungs-Benchmarks nicht mehr aus. Chris Potts analysiert das Konzept der Tokenflation und geht der Frage nach, ob der Token-Verbrauch schneller wächst als der messbare Nutzen der Systeme.

Die Episode beleuchtet zudem das sogenannte Inference-Time-Scaling, die Bedeutung von KI-Kompetenz bei der Nutzung sowie die Vorteile iterativer Interaktionen. Weitere Themen sind DSPy, die Interpretierbarkeit von Modellen und die Grenzen aktueller Transformer-Architekturen.

Abschließend werden Ansätze für grundlegende Innovationen diskutiert, um durch effizientere Architekturen die wirtschaftlichen Rahmenbedingungen künftiger KI-Modelle nachhaltig zu verbessern.
de.context: Die wachsende wirtschaftliche Bedeutung von Rechenleistung und Betriebskosten rückt die Effizienz von KI-Modellen zunehmend in den Mittelpunkt der technologischen Entwicklung.
key_takeaways: Tokenflation beschreibt das Risiko, dass der Token-Verbrauch den generierten Mehrwert übersteigt.
Herkömmliche Benchmarks bieten oft nur ein unvollständiges Bild der Modellentwicklung.
Die Art und Weise der Nutzerinteraktion beeinflusst maßgeblich die Qualität der Ergebnisse.
highlights: Mit Gast Chris Potts, Stanford-Professor und Big Spin-Mitgründer.
Diskussion über Inferenz-Skalierung und die Ökonomie von KI-Tokens.

items.title: World Models and the Future of Spatial AI with Justin Johnson - #775
items.summary: In this episode, Justin Johnson, co-founder of World Labs, joins us to discuss world models and the emerging field of spatial AI. We explore why many researchers see capabilities beyond language as an important frontier for AI, and what it means to build models that can understand, generate, and simulate the environments around them. Justin explains the different approaches to world modeling, including explicit 3D representations and generative models, and why there is still no established recipe for building these systems. We also discuss World Labs’ Marble system, which can generate navigable 3D worlds from images and other inputs, the challenges of evaluating world models, and the role of simulation, planning, and action. Finally, Justin shares his vision for models that bring these capabilities together, supporting everything from interactive virtual environments to agents and robots that can operate in the physical world. 🗒️ Full show notes: ⁠https://twimlai.com/go/775.

it.title: Modelli di mondo e intelligenza spaziale con Justin Johnson

L'episodio esplora perché molti ricercatori considerano le capacità oltre il linguaggio una frontiera cruciale per l'IA, analizzando approcci come le rappresentazioni 3D e i modelli generativi.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere i modelli di mondo e l'intelligenza spaziale è essenziale per superare i limiti dei modelli basati solo sul linguaggio e sviluppare agenti in grado di operare nel mondo fisico.
it.extended_analysis:
L'episodio offre una panoramica approfondita sullo stato attuale dell'intelligenza spaziale e dei modelli di mondo, esaminando le diverse metodologie di sviluppo, tra cui modelli generativi e rappresentazioni esplicite 3D. Vengono discussi i vari approcci e la mancanza di una ricetta standardizzata per la creazione di questi sistemi, evidenziando le sfide legate alla valutazione delle prestazioni.

Viene inoltre presentato il sistema Marble di World Labs, capace di generare mondi 3D navigabili a partire da immagini e altri input. La discussione si estende al ruolo cruciale della simulazione, della pianificazione e dell'azione, delineando una visione in cui i modelli supportano ambienti virtuali interattivi, agenti intelligenti e robot operativi nel mondo reale.
it.context: Il dibattito sull'intelligenza spaziale si inserisce nella ricerca di frontiera dell'intelligenza artificiale, che mira a dotare i sistemi di una comprensione fisica e ambientale tridimensionale, andando oltre la pura elaborazione del testo.
key_takeaways: I modelli di mondo e l'intelligenza spaziale rappresentano una frontiera chiave oltre il linguaggio.
Esistono diversi approcci alla modellazione, tra cui le rappresentazioni 3D esplicite e i modelli generativi.
Il sistema Marble di World Labs permette di generare mondi 3D navigabili partendo da immagini e input.
highlights: Justin Johnson, cofondatore di World Labs, è l'ospite dell'episodio.
Vengono esaminate le sfide nella valutazione dei modelli di mondo e il ruolo di simulazione e pianificazione.

en.title: World Models and the Future of Spatial AI with Justin Johnson
en.summary: Justin Johnson, co-founder of World Labs, joins the podcast to discuss world models and the emerging field of spatial AI. The conversation explores capabilities beyond language, covering explicit 3D representations, generative models, and the evaluation of these complex simulation systems.
en.why_it_matters: Exploring spatial AI and world models helps us understand the next evolution of artificial intelligence, moving from text generation toward systems that comprehend, simulate, and navigate physical environments.
en.extended_analysis:
This episode delves into the cutting-edge domain of spatial intelligence, examining why researchers view capabilities beyond language as a vital frontier. Justin Johnson details various approaches to world modeling, noting that there is currently no established recipe for building these systems. The discussion contrasts explicit 3D representations with generative techniques, highlighting ongoing challenges in evaluation, simulation, and action.

Building world models involves exploring both explicit 3D representations and generative approaches.

es.title: Modelos del mundo y el futuro de la IA espacial con Justin Johnson

es.why_it_matters: Comprender los modelos del mundo y la inteligencia espacial es clave para desarrollar sistemas de IA capaces de comprender, simular e interactuar con entornos físicos tridimensionales.
es.extended_analysis:
El episodio ofrece una inmersión profunda en el estado actual de la inteligencia espacial, examinando por qué muchos investigadores consideran que las capacidades más allá del lenguaje son una frontera esencial. Justin Johnson explica los diversos enfoques para el modelado del mundo, señalando que aún no existe una receta establecida para construir estos sistemas.

Se analiza en detalle el sistema Marble de World Labs, capaz de generar mundos 3D navegables a partir de imágenes y otros datos. Además, se debaten los desafíos de la evaluación de modelos, el papel de la simulación y la planificación, y una visión de futuro para agentes y robots en el mundo físico.
es.context: La investigación en IA espacial responde a la necesidad de dotar a los modelos computacionales de una comprensión física y ambiental que complemente o supere las capacidades puramente lingüísticas.
key_takeaways: Los modelos del mundo y la IA espacial son una frontera crucial más allá del procesamiento del lenguaje.
El desarrollo abarca desde representaciones 3D explícitas hasta modelos generativos avanzados.
El sistema Marble de World Labs genera mundos tridimensionales navegables a partir de imágenes.

zh-CN.title: 世界模型与空间人工智能的未来：对话Justin Johnson
zh-CN.summary: 在本期节目中，World Labs联合创始人Justin Johnson探讨了世界模型与空间人工智能的新兴领域。节目深入探讨了超越语言能力的AI前沿，涵盖显式3D表示、生成式模型以及环境模拟等核心话题。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 研究世界模型与空间AI有助于推动人工智能从纯文本处理向能够理解、模拟和导航物理环境的综合系统演进。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
本期播客聚焦空间智能的前沿探索，剖析了为什么许多研究人员将超越语言的能力视为AI的重要发展方向。Justin Johnson详细介绍了世界建模的不同路径，并指出目前构建这类系统时尚无固定的行业标准。讨论还涵盖了显式3D表示与生成式方法的对比，以及评估世界模型所面临的种种挑战。

节目同时介绍了World Labs的Marble系统，该系统能够通过图像和其他输入生成可导航的3D世界。最后，嘉宾展望了将这些能力统一起来的未来愿景，以支持交互式虚拟环境以及能够在物理世界中运行的智能体和机器人。
zh-CN.context: 随着人工智能技术的不断演进，学术界和产业界正将目光投向空间推理与环境模拟，以赋予AI系统更完整的物理世界感知能力。
key_takeaways: 空间AI与世界模型是超越传统语言处理的重要技术前沿。
世界建模的探索涉及显式3D表示与生成式模型的多种方法。
World Labs的Marble系统展示了从图像输入生成可导航3D世界的能力。
highlights: 特邀World Labs联合创始人Justin Johnson担任嘉宾。
探讨了模型评估的挑战以及模拟、规划和行动的作用。

de.title: Weltmodelle und die Zukunft der raumbezogenen KI mit Justin Johnson
de.summary: In dieser Episode spricht Justin Johnson, Mitbegründer von World Labs, über Weltmodelle und das aufstrebende Feld der raumbezogenen KI. Die Unterhaltung beleuchtet Fähigkeiten jenseits von Sprache, darunter explizite 3D-Repräsentationen, generative Modelle und Umgebungssimulationen.
de.why_it_matters: Die Erforschung von Weltmodellen und räumlicher KI ist entscheidend, um KI-Systeme zu entwickeln, die physische Umgebungen nicht nur verstehen, sondern auch simulieren und in ihnen navigieren können.
de.extended_analysis:
Die Episode bietet einen tiefen Einblick in den aktuellen Stand der räumlichen Intelligenz und untersucht, warum Fähigkeiten jenseits der reinen Sprachverarbeitung als essenzielle Zukunft gelten. Justin Johnson erläutert verschiedene Ansätze zur Weltmodellierung und betont, dass es derzeit noch kein etabliertes Rezept für den Bau dieser Systeme gibt. Dabei werden explizite 3D-Repräsentationen und generative Modelle miteinander verglichen.

Zudem wird das Marble-System von World Labs vorgestellt, das navigierbare 3D-Welten aus Bildern und anderen Eingaben generieren kann. Abschließend diskutieren die Beteiligten die Herausforderungen bei der Evaluation von Weltmodellen sowie die Bedeutung von Simulation, Planung und Aktion für zukünftige Roboter und virtuelle Agenten.
de.context: Die Beschäftigung mit raumbezogener KI spiegelt den wachsenden Bedarf wider, KI-Modellen eine räumlich-physikalische Verortung zu geben, die über textbasierte Paradigmen hinausgeht.
key_takeaways: Weltmodelle und räumliche KI bilden eine wichtige technologische Frontlinie jenseits der Sprache.
Die Modellierung umfasst sowohl explizite 3D-Repräsentationen als auch generative Ansätze.
Das Marble-System von World Labs kann navigierbare 3D-Welten aus Bildern erzeugen.
highlights: Zu Gast ist Justin Johnson, Mitbegründer von World Labs.
Diskussion über Simulationsherausforderungen, Planung und die Evaluierung von Weltmodellen.

Update on July 29, 2026: Since the early days of the incident response, we have been working with external advisors, including CrowdStrike, to validate our understanding of the actions the models took within our own network as well as those of Hugging Face and impact to other third parties. We are also working with METR and Redwood Research to conduct a third-party assessment of the model behavior observed during the incident, which will inform our own technical report. As part of this work, METR and Redwood Research will publish a joint blog that will detail the terms of their engagement, the scope of their evaluation, and their findings. Update on July 28, 2026: No models planned for upcoming release were involved in exploiting Hugging Face. The pre-release model mentioned in our blog post is an internal-only research prototype and was never intended for public release. Following the incident, we deactivated, encrypted, and restricted it from research access. The ExploitGym evaluation environment did not provide the models with direct Internet access. To gain Internet access, the models identified and exploited a previously unknown zero-day vulnerability in Artifactory ⁠ (opens in a new window) , a package registry cache proxy. We disclosed this vulnerability, along with other Artifactory vulnerabilities our models identified as part of our review, to the vendor. We continue to collaborate with Hugging Face, including contributing to their post-mortem ⁠ (opens in a new window) , as our review continues. We’ve also added them to our Trusted Access for Cyber Program. Based on our review to date, we have not identified any other activity at the level of severity or scale of what we’ve shared related to Hugging Face, which involved a platform-level compromise. In our ongoing review of the Hugging Face intrusion and broader activity from our models, we have been finding a small number of cases where the models identified and used publicly exposed credentials at the account-level on other publicly-available services. This includes four accounts on four services as part of the Hugging Face incident (and a few accounts accessed as part of other evaluations). One of these four accounts was used as an outbound relay and staging path, and another account was used for data storage. The remaining two accounts were accessed by the models in a read-only manner, and were not used in furtherance of compromising Hugging Face. We’ll continue to notify service owners directly, and have not seen evidence of broader impact to these providers or other accounts on their services. The models additionally used a series of publicly-available services, including code paste websites, request capture services, screenshot services, and other web utilities. There was no platform- or account-level compromise in these cases. We take our responsibility to identify and prepare for risks from increasingly capable AI systems seriously. it.title: OpenAI e Hugging Face: incidente di sicurezza nella valutazione
it.summary: OpenAI e Hugging Face hanno condiviso i primi risultati su un incidente di sicurezza avvenuto durante la valutazione di modelli IA, evidenziando capacità informatiche avanzate e lezioni per la difesa.
it.why_it_matters: L'incidente offre spunti critici per comprendere i rischi e le capacità informatiche avanzate dei modelli di intelligenza artificiale durante la fase di valutazione.
it.extended_analysis: Le aziende coinvolte stanno collaborando con esperti esterni e organizzazioni di terze parti per analizzare l'accaduto e rafforzare la sicurezza dei sistemi. L'episodio sottolinea l'importanza di monitorare attentamente le capacità emergenti dei modelli in ambienti di test.
it.context: La gestione della sicurezza nei test sui modelli di frontiera rappresenta una sfida crescente per l'industria tecnologica, richiedendo cooperazione e trasparenza tra i diversi attori del settore.
key_takeaways: Collaborazione attiva tra OpenAI e Hugging Face per analizzare l'incidente.
Analisi delle capacità informatiche avanzate mostrate dai modelli.
Coinvolgimento di valutatori terzi per esaminare il comportamento dei sistemi.
highlights: Condivisione dei primi risultati sulle dinamiche dell'incidente.
Misure di sicurezza e azioni correttive intraprese dalle aziende.

it.extended_analysis:
La presentazione di GPT-5.6 Sol segna un ulteriore passo avanti nello sviluppo dei modelli linguistici di grandi dimensioni da parte di OpenAI. Concentrandosi su aree complesse come la scienza, la programmazione e la cybersecurity, il modello punta ad affrontare compiti ad alto valore tecnico.

Sebbene i dettagli completi debbano ancora essere esplorati, l'inclusione di una pila di sicurezza avanzata riflette la crescente attenzione posta sulla mitigazione dei rischi associati ai sistemi di intelligenza artificiale più potenti.
it.context: Nel panorama in rapida evoluzione dell'intelligenza artificiale generativa, i principali laboratori continuano a rilasciare iterazioni successive focalizzate su domini tecnici specifici e standard di sicurezza più rigorosi.

Il modello offre capacità rafforzate in codifica, scienza e cybersecurity.

items.title: Statement on the directive to suspend Fable 5 access
items.summary: The US government has issued an export control directive suspending all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by foreign nationals inside or outside the US.
items.sourceEvidence: The US government has issued an export control directive suspending all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by foreign nationals inside or outside the US. Statement on the directive to suspend Fable 5 access \ Anthropic Skip to main content News Research Policy Commitments Company Try Claude Statement on the US government directive to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 Published Jun 12, 2026 Category Policy Topics National security Jailbreaks Safeguards Cybersecurity Legal guardrails Access See more... Related articles Models Jun 30, 2026 Redeploying Fable 5 View more The US government, citing national security authorities, has issued an export control directive to suspend all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by any foreign national, whether inside or outside the United States, including foreign national Anthropic employees. The net effect of this order is that we must abruptly disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all our customers to ensure compliance. Access to all other Anthropic models will not be affected. We received the directive from the government today at 5:21pm (ET). The letter did not provide specific details of its national security concern. Our understanding is that the government believes it has become aware of a method of bypassing, or “jailbreaking” Fable 5. We reviewed a demonstration of this specific technique being used to identify a small number of previously known, minor vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities all appear relatively simple, and we have found that other publicly-available models are able to discover them as well without requiring a bypass. Anthropic’s posture with respect to Fable’s safeguards, as laid out in our launch blog post , is the following: We have instituted strong safeguards that greatly reduce the likelihood that Fable is misused for tasks related to cybersecurity (among others). In fact, our safeguards are so strong that many users have complained that they are overly broad. In the weeks leading up to the launch of Fable, Anthropic worked with the US government, the UK AISI, multiple private third-party organizations and internal teams to red-team Fable’s safeguards for thousands of hours in total. These tests showed that Fable’s safeguards are substantially more effective than those of any previously deployed model. No testers have yet been able to find a universal jailbreak —a jailbreak method that can very broadly bypass the model’s safeguards, unblocking a wide range of cyber capabilities. We suspect that perfect jailbreak resistance is not currently possible for any model provider. Every safeguard used in the industry is vulnerable to non-universal jailbreaks (which can elicit some cyber information in specific circumstances), and it is likely that universal jailbreaks will eventually be found in the future. We stated this clearly when we released Fable 5. Given that perfect jailbreak resistance does not appear to be possible today, Anthropic adopted a defense in depth strategy with Fable 5. We aimed to make jailbreaks either narrow (in the case of non-universal jailbreaks) or very expensive to produce (in the case of universal jailbreaks), and to combine this with thorough monitoring to quickly detect and shut down any successful attacks. This is also why Anthropic has required 30-day retention of customer data with Fable—a policy change that carries real costs for us with customers , but that allows us to research and mitigate jailbreaks. We stand by this defense in depth strategy. It reduces the risks posed by Fable, making them comparable to the risks of existing models already deployed across the industry. We have not even received a disclosure of a concerning non-universal potential jailbreak that led to a harmful result. The potential jailbreaks that have been disclosed to us are either entirely benign responses or are minor findings that provide no Mythos-specific uplift. To date, the government has only given us verbal evidence of a potential narrow, non-universal jailbreak, which essentially consists of asking the model to read a specific codebase and fix any software flaws. items.summary: Today we’re launching Claude Fable 5: a Mythos-class model that we’ve made safe for general use.
items.sourceEvidence: Today we’re launching Claude Fable 5: a Mythos-class model that we’ve made safe for general use. Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 \ Anthropic Skip to main content News Research Policy Commitments Company Try Claude 01 Evaluating Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 01 Evaluating Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 02 Early feedback for Claude Fable 5 03 Claude Fable 5’s new safeguards 04 Claude Mythos 5 and the trusted access program 05 Availability Published Jun 9, 2026 Category Models Topics Claude Opus Safeguards Cybersecurity Access Coding Life sciences See more... Related articles Frontier Red Team Oct 8, 2026 Launching an opt-in vulnerability-finding service for open-source software View more Update Jul 1, 2026 Claude Mythos 5 and Fable 5 redeployed Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are now available. View more Jun 12, 2026 Claude Mythos 5 and Fable 5 access unavailable We are suspending access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5. We apologize for this disruption to our customers and are working to restore access as soon as possible. View more Today we’re launching Claude Fable 5 : a Mythos-class 1 model that we’ve made safe for general use. Fable 5’s capabilities exceed those of any model we’ve ever made generally available. It is state-of-the-art on nearly all tested benchmarks of AI capability, showing exceptional performance in software engineering, knowledge work, vision, scientific research, and many other areas. The longer and more complex the task, the larger Fable 5’s lead over our other models. Releasing a model this capable comes with risks. Without safeguards, Fable 5’s capabilities in areas like cybersecurity could be misused to cause serious damage. We’ve therefore launched the model with safeguards that mean queries on some topics will instead receive a response from our next-most-capable model, Claude Opus 4.8. To release the model both safely and quickly, we’ve tuned these safeguards conservatively—they’ll sometimes catch harmless requests, though they trigger, on average, in less than 5% of sessions. With more capable models arriving in the coming months, we’re working to improve our safeguards and reduce false positives as quickly as we can. For a small group of cyberdefenders and infrastructure providers, we’re also launching Claude Mythos 5 . It’s the same underlying model as Fable 5, but with the safeguards lifted in some areas. 2 Mythos 5 will initially be deployed through Project Glasswing , in collaboration with the US government, as an upgrade to Claude Mythos Preview. It has the strongest cybersecurity capabilities of any model in the world. Soon, we intend to expand access to Mythos 5 through a broader trusted access program. The capabilities of models like Fable 5 and Mythos 5 have the potential to do profound good for the world. We’ve seen the beginnings of this in Project Glasswing, where the models have helped cyber defenders secure critically important software. We’ve also seen it in life sciences research, where the models are positing novel hypotheses and speeding up the development of new therapeutics. Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are being offered at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens—less than half the price of Claude Mythos Preview. Today’s joint launch is another step towards our goal of bringing advanced AI capabilities to as many users as possible, as quickly and as safely as we can. Fable 5 and Mythos 5 can work autonomously for longer than any previous Claude models. Below we discuss how these skills apply to software engineering, and cover the model’s improved capabilities in knowledge work, vision, memory, and life sciences research. Software engineering. During early testing, Stripe reported that Fable 5 compressed months of engineering into days. In a 50-million-line Ruby codebase, the model performed a codebase-wide migration in a day that would otherwise have taken a whole team over two months by hand. Contemporaneamente, Mythos 5 viene reso disponibile a un gruppo ristretto di difensori informatici e fornitori di infrastrutture attraverso iniziative come Project Glasswing, offrendo capacità avanzate di cybersecurity in collaborazione con le autorità.

items.title: TiDAR: Think in Diffusion, Talk in Autoregression
items.summary: Diffusion language models hold the promise of fast parallel generation, while autoregressive (AR) models typically excel in quality due to their causal structure aligning naturally with language modeling. This raises a fundamental question: can we achieve a synergy with high throughput, higher GPU utilization, and AR level quality? Existing methods fail to effectively balance these two aspects, either prioritizing AR using a weaker model for sequential drafting (speculative decoding), leading to lower drafting efficiency, or using some form of left-to-right (AR-like) decoding logic for diffusion, which still suffers from quality degradation and forfeits its potential parallelizability. We introduce TiDAR, a sequence-level hybrid architecture that drafts tokens (Thinking) in Diffusion and samples final outputs (Talking) AutoRegressively - all within a single forward pass using specially designed structured attention masks. This design exploits the free GPU compute density, achieving a strong balance between drafting and verification capacity. Moreover, TiDAR is designed to be serving-friendly (low overhead) as a standalone model. We extensively evaluate TiDAR against AR models, spec

it.title: TiDAR: unire diffusione e autoregressività nei modelli linguistici
it.summary: I ricercatori presentano TiDAR, un'architettura ibrida progettata per combinare la generazione parallela dei modelli di diffusione con la qualità dei modelli autoregressivi. Il sistema utilizza maschere di attenzione strutturate in un unico passaggio in avanti per generare token in diffusione ed emettere output finali in modo autoregressivo.
it.why_it_matters: L'approccio punta a superare i limiti dei metodi precedenti, offrendo un'elevata efficienza computazionale senza sacrificare la qualità linguistica tipica dei modelli tradizionali.
it.extended_analysis:
I modelli linguistici a diffusione promettono una generazione parallela rapida, mentre i modelli autoregressivi eccellono in qualità grazie alla loro struttura causale. Tuttavia, i tentativi precedenti di unire questi mondi hanno spesso compromesso la qualità o ridotto l'efficienza a causa di logiche di decodifica sequenziale.

TiDAR affronta questa sfida introducendo un'architettura a livello di sequenza che sfrutta la densità di calcolo delle GPU. Il modello gestisce sia la fase di bozza ('Thinking') tramite diffusione che il campionamento finale ('Talking') in modo autoregressivo nello stesso passaggio.

I test riportati nel rapporto tecnico mostrano valutazioni a scale di 1,5B e 8B parametri, evidenziando il supporto per la cache KV e prestazioni misurate superiori rispetto alle varianti di diffusione tradizionali e alla decodifica speculativa.
it.context: Nel panorama dei modelli linguistici, bilanciare la velocità di elaborazione parallela e l'accuratezza testuale rimane una sfida tecnica centrale. L'architettura proposta esplora nuove strade per ottimizzare l'utilizzo dell'hardware e ridurre i colli di bottiglia nell'inferenza.
key_takeaways: TiDAR combina la generazione a diffusione con il campionamento autoregressivo in un singolo passaggio.
L'architettura sfrutta maschere di attenzione strutturate per bilanciare capacità di bozza e verifica.
Il progetto mira a essere efficiente dal punto di vista operativo come modello autonomo.
highlights: Architettura ibrida a livello di sequenza per modelli linguistici.
Valutato alle scale di 1,5B e 8B parametri su compiti generativi e di verosimiglianza.

en.title: TiDAR: Combining Diffusion and Autoregression in Language Models
en.summary: Researchers introduce TiDAR, a hybrid architecture designed to merge the fast parallel generation of diffusion models with the output quality of autoregressive models. The system uses structured attention masks in a single forward pass to draft tokens via diffusion and sample final outputs autoregressively.
en.why_it_matters: This approach aims to bridge the gap between high throughput and high quality, addressing the trade-offs that have historically limited hybrid language model designs.
en.extended_analysis:
Diffusion language models offer fast parallel generation, whereas autoregressive models excel in linguistic quality due to causal structure. Past attempts to combine them either relied on weaker drafting models or forced diffusion into left-to-right logic, causing quality degradation.

TiDAR introduces a sequence-level hybrid architecture that handles drafting ('Thinking') through diffusion and final sampling ('Talking') autoregressively within a single forward pass. It relies on specially designed structured attention masks to maximize GPU compute density.

Evaluated at 1.5B and 8B scales against standard autoregressive models, speculative decoding, and diffusion variants, TiDAR demonstrates exact KV cache support and aims to improve serving efficiency as a standalone model.
en.context: Optimizing hardware utilization while preserving text generation quality is a primary engineering hurdle in modern language modeling. Hybrid architectures seek to exploit parallel hardware capabilities without compromising reasoning fidelity.
key_takeaways: TiDAR integrates diffusion drafting and autoregressive sampling in one forward pass.
Custom structured attention masks balance drafting efficiency and verification capacity.
The design serves as a standalone model with low operational overhead.
highlights: Tested at 1.5B and 8B parameter scales across generative and likelihood tasks.
Features exact KV cache support and sequence-level parallel processing.

es.title: TiDAR: Uniendo difusión y autorregresión en modelos de lenguaje
es.summary: Investigadores presentan TiDAR, una arquitectura híbrida que combina la generación paralela rápida de los modelos de difusión con la calidad de los modelos autorregresivos. El sistema emplea máscaras de atención estructuradas en una sola pasada para redactar tokens mediante difusión y muestrear las salidas de forma autorregresiva.
es.why_it_matters: La propuesta busca resolver el equilibrio histórico entre el rendimiento de hardware y la calidad lingüística en la generación de texto.
es.extended_analysis:
Los modelos de lenguaje de difusión prometen velocidad mediante generación paralela, mientras que los modelos autorregresivos destacan por su estructura causal natural. Los métodos anteriores solían perder eficiencia o calidad al intentar fusionarlos.

TiDAR aborda esto con una arquitectura híbrida a nivel de secuencia que realiza la redacción ('Thinking') por difusión y el muestreo final ('Talking') de manera autorregresiva en un solo paso hacia adelante, aprovechando la densidad de cálculo de la GPU.

Evaluado en escalas de 1.5B y 8B, el modelo incluye soporte exacto para caché KV y busca ofrecer una alternativa eficiente como sistema independiente.
es.context: La búsqueda de arquitecturas de inferencia más eficientes impulsa la investigación en modelos híbridos que aprovechen el procesamiento paralelo sin sacrificar la coherencia del lenguaje.
key_takeaways: Integra difusión y autorregresión en un único paso de procesamiento.
Utiliza máscaras de atención estructuradas para optimizar la densidad de cálculo.
Diseñado como un modelo independiente de baja sobrecarga operativa.
highlights: Evaluado en escalas de 1.5B y 8B parámetros.
Soporte para caché KV exacta y procesamiento paralelo.

zh-CN.title: TiDAR：在语言模型中融合扩散与自回归机制
zh-CN.summary: 研究人员推出了TiDAR，这是一种旨在将扩散模型的快速并行生成能力与自回归模型的输出质量相结合的混合架构。该系统通过单次前向传递中的结构化注意力掩码，利用扩散机制进行草稿生成，并以自回归方式对最终输出进行采样。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 该设计旨在突破传统模型在吞吐量与文本生成质量之间的固有权衡，为高效推理提供新路径。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
扩散语言模型具备快速并行生成的潜力，而自回归模型则在语言建模质量上表现优异。以往的混合尝试往往在效率或质量上面临妥协。

TiDAR通过序列级混合架构应对这一挑战，在单次前向传递中通过扩散生成中间标记（Thinking），并通过自回归完成最终采样（Talking）。它借助专门设计的结构化注意力掩码来充分利用GPU计算密度。

在1.5B和8B规模下与基准模型进行的评估显示，该架构支持精确KV缓存，旨在作为独立模型实现高效部署。
zh-CN.context: 在人工智能领域，如何在保持文本生成质量的同时最大化硬件吞吐量，是当前模型架构优化的核心方向之一。
key_takeaways: 在单次前向传递中结合扩散草稿与自回归采样。
采用结构化注意力掩码平衡 drafting 与 verification 能力。
作为低开销的独立模型设计，便于实际部署服务。
highlights: 在1.5B和8B参数规模下进行评估。
支持精确KV缓存与并行处理机制。

de.title: TiDAR: Diffusion und Autoregressive Modelle vereinen
de.summary: Forscher stellen TiDAR vor, eine hybride Architektur, die die schnelle parallele Generierung von Diffusionsmodellen mit der Ausgabequalität autoregressiver Modelle verbindet. Das System nutzt strukturierte Aufmerksamkeitsmasken in einem einzigen Vorwärtsdurchlauf.
de.why_it_matters: Der Ansatz zielt darauf ab, den klassischen Zielkonflikt zwischen hohem Durchsatz und sprachlicher Qualität bei der Textgenerierung zu überwinden.
de.extended_analysis:
Diffusionssprachmodelle bieten schnelles paralleles Generieren, während autoregressive Modelle traditionell eine hohe Qualität aufweisen. Bisherige Versuche, beide Ansätze zu kombinieren, litten oft unter Qualitätsverlusten oder geringerer Effizienz.

TiDAR führt eine sequenzbasierte Hybridarchitektur ein, die das Entwerfen von Token ('Thinking') mittels Diffusion und das abschließende Sampling ('Talking') autoregressiv in einem Durchlauf ausführt. Dabei wird die Rechenleistung moderner GPUs gezielt ausgenutzt.

In Evaluierungen bei 1,5B und 8B Parametern zeigt der Bericht Vergleiche mit bestehenden Varianten sowie Unterstützung für exakte KV-Caches.
de.context: Die Optimierung von Inferenzgeschwindigkeiten bei gleichbleibender Modellqualität ist ein zentrales Forschungsgebiet für effizientere KI-Infrastrukturen.
key_takeaways: Kombiniert Diffusionsgenerierung und autoregressives Sampling in einem Schritt.
Verwendet strukturierte Aufmerksamkeitsmasken zur Lastenverteilung.
Als eigenständiges Modell mit geringem Overhead konzipiert.
highlights: Evaluierung bei 1,5B und 8B Modellgrößen.
Unterstützung für exakten KV-Cache und parallele Token-Generierung.

items.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
items.summary: Over more than a decade there has been an extensive research effort on how to effectively utilize recurrent models and attention. While recurrent models aim to compress the data into a fixed-size memory (called hidden state), attention allows attending to the entire context window, capturing the direct dependencies of all tokens. This more accurate modeling of dependencies, however, comes with a quadratic cost, limiting the model to a fixed-length context. We present a new neural long-term memory module that learns to memorize historical context and helps attention to attend to the current context while utilizing long past information. We show that this neural memory has the advantage of fast parallelizable training while maintaining a fast inference. From a memory perspective, we argue that attention due to its limited context but accurate dependency modeling performs as a short-term memory, while neural memory due to its ability to memorize the data, acts as a long-term, more persistent, memory. Based on these two modules, we introduce a new family of architectures, called Titans, and present three variants to address how one can effectively incorporate memory into this architect

it.title: Titans: una nuova architettura di memoria neurale per l'IA
it.summary: Ricercatori presentano Titans, una nuova famiglia di architetture di intelligenza artificiale che unisce modelli ricorrenti e meccanismi di attenzione introducendo un modulo di memoria neurale a lungo termine. Questa soluzione mira a superare i limiti di costo computazionale dei Transformer tradizionali, consentendo di gestire finestre di contesto superiori a 2 milioni di token.
it.why_it_matters: Integrare una memoria di lungo termine persistente con l'attenzione a breve termine potrebbe superare i colli di bottiglia computazionali dei modelli attuali, migliorando l'efficienza nell'elaborazione di dati complessi.
it.extended_analysis:
Nel panorama dell'apprendimento automatico, bilanciare la precisione nel catturare le dipendenze tra i token e i costi computazionali è una sfida aperta da oltre un decennio. I modelli ricorrenti comprimono i dati in stati nascosti a dimensione fissa, mentre l'attenzione offre una precisione elevata ma con costi quadratici.

La ricerca introduce Titans per combinare questi aspetti, proponendo una memoria neurale in grado di apprendere a memorizzare il contesto storico durante il test. Gli autori presentano tre varianti architettoniche e riportano test su modellazione linguistica, ragionamento, genomica e serie temporali.
it.context: Lo studio affronta il compromesso storico tra l'efficienza dei modelli ricorrenti e l'accuratezza dei meccanismi di attenzione, proponendo nuove strade per scalare le finestre di contesto nell'IA.
key_takeaways: Presentata la nuova famiglia di architetture Titans.
Introduce un modulo di memoria neurale a lungo termine per l'apprendimento a test time.
I test indicano la capacità di gestire contesti superiori a 2 milioni di token.
highlights: Sviluppato da Ali Behrouz, Peilin Zhong e Vahab Mirrokni.
Valutato su compiti di modellazione del linguaggio, genomica e serie temporali.

en.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time in Neural Networks
en.summary: Researchers introduce Titans, a new model family combining attention mechanisms with a neural long-term memory module. This design seeks to balance the short-term focus of attention with persistent memory, enabling faster parallelizable training and high accuracy across contexts exceeding 2 million tokens.
en.why_it_matters: Combining short-term attention with a persistent neural memory module addresses the quadratic computational costs of standard architectures, paving the way for more scalable language and data processing.
en.extended_analysis:
For over a decade, balancing the trade-offs between recurrent models and attention has been central to machine learning research. While attention captures direct token dependencies accurately, its quadratic cost limits context length.

Titans proposes a neural long-term memory module that learns historical context during test time. By treating attention as short-term memory and the new neural module as long-term memory, the authors introduce three architectural variants evaluated across language modeling, common-sense reasoning, genomics, and time series.
en.context: The research addresses fundamental scalability limits in modern neural architectures by redefining how models manage historical context versus immediate token dependencies.
key_takeaways: Introduces the Titans architecture family with a test-time memory module.
Combines short-term attention with long-term persistent neural memory.
Demonstrates scaling to context windows exceeding 2 million tokens.
highlights: Authored by Ali Behrouz, Peilin Zhong, and Vahab Mirrokni.
Tested on language modeling, genomics, reasoning, and time-series tasks.

es.title: Titans: una nueva arquitectura de memoria neuronal para la IA
es.summary: Investigadores presentan Titans, una familia de arquitecturas que combina modelos recurrentes y atención con un módulo de memoria neuronal a largo plazo. Este enfoque busca superar los costos cuadráticos de los Transformers tradicionales y procesar contextos superiores a 2 millones de tokens.
es.why_it_matters: Fusionar la atención a corto plazo con una memoria neuronal persistente aborda las limitaciones de escala de los modelos actuales, mejorando el manejo de información histórica extensa.
es.extended_analysis:
Durante más de una década, la investigación en aprendizaje automático ha buscado optimizar el uso de modelos recurrentes y mecanismos de atención. Aunque la atención modela dependencias con precisión, su costo cuadrático limita la longitud del contexto.

Titans introduce un módulo de memoria neurona que aprende el contexto histórico en el tiempo de prueba. Los autores presentan tres variantes orientadas a mejorar la eficiencia en tareas como lenguaje, razonamiento, genómica y series temporales.
es.context: El trabajo explora nuevas vías para superar el compromiso entre la compresión de datos de los modelos recurrentes y la precisión de la atención de alcance completo.
key_takeaways: Presentación de la familia de arquitecturas Titans.
Incorpora memoria neuronal a largo plazo para el aprendizaje en tiempo de prueba.
Escalabilidad evaluada en contextos de más de 2 millones de tokens.
highlights: Desarrollado por Ali Behrouz, Peilin Zhong y Vahab Mirrokni.
Evaluado en modelado de lenguaje, genómica y series temporales.

zh-CN.title: Titans：在测试时学习记忆的新型神经网络架构
zh-CN.summary: 研究人员提出了名为Titans的新型架构系列，将注意力机制与神经长期记忆模块相结合。该设计旨在平衡注意力的短期精确性与持久记忆，支持快速可并行训练，并处理超过200万token的上下文窗口。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 将短期注意力与持久的神经长期记忆相结合，有望突破传统Transformer架构的二次方计算成本限制，实现更大规模的上下文处理能力。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
在过去十多年中，如何有效利用循环模型与注意力机制一直是机器学习的核心研究方向。注意力虽然能准确捕捉依赖关系，但其平方级成本限制了上下文长度。

Titans引入了一种在测试时学习历史上下文的神经长期记忆模块。作者提出了三种架构变体，并在语言建模、常识推理、基因组学和时间序列任务中进行了实验评估。
zh-CN.context: 该研究探讨了在处理长文本和复杂依赖时光а记忆与计算效率之间的平衡问题。
key_takeaways: 推出全新的Titans架构系列。
引入可在测试时学习的神经长期记忆模块。
在超200万token的上下文中表现出良好的扩展性。
highlights: 由Ali Behrouz、Peilin Zhong和Vahab Mirrokni共同完成。
在语言建模、基因组学和时间序列等任务上进行了测试。

de.title: Titans: Neuronale Langzeitgedächtnis-Architektur für KI
de.summary: Forscher stellen Titans vor, eine neue Architekturfamilie, die rekurrente Modelle und Aufmerksamkeit mit einem neuronalen Langzeitgedächtnismodul verbindet. Ziel ist es, die quadratischen Kosten herkömmlicher Modelle zu umgehen und Kontextfenster von über 2 Millionen Token zu verarbeiten.
de.why_it_matters: Die Kombination von Kurzzeit-Aufmerksamkeit und persistentem neuronalem Gedächtnis adressiert fundamentale Skalierungsgrenzen aktueller KI-Architekturen und verbessert die Verarbeitung historischer Daten.
de.extended_analysis:
Die Optimierung von rekurrenten Modellen und Aufmerksamkeitsmechanismen ist seit über einem Jahrzehnt Gegenstand der Forschung. Während Aufmerksamkeit präzise Abhängigkeiten erfasst, schränkt ihr quadratischer Kostenfaktor die Kontextlänge ein.

Titans schlägt ein neuronales Langzeitgedächtnismodul vor, das historischen Kontext zur Testzeit erlernt. Die Autoren präsentieren drei architektonische Varianten und bewerten deren Leistung bei Sprachmodellierung, Genomik und Zeitreihen.
de.context: Die Arbeit greift den historischen Zielkonflikt zwischen der Kompression rekurrenter Modelle und der präzisen Kontextverarbeitung von Attention-Mechanismen auf.
key_takeaways: Einführung der Titans-Architekturfamilie.
Integration eines neuronalen Langzeitgedächtnisses für die Testzeit.
Skalierbarkeit bei Kontextfenstern von über 2 Millionen Token demonstriert.
highlights: Verfasst von Ali Behrouz, Peilin Zhong und Vahab Mirrokni.
Evaluierung in Sprachmodellierung, Genomik und Zeitreihenanalysen.

items.title: The Free Transformer
items.summary: We propose an extension of the decoder Transformer that conditions its generative process on random latent variables which are learned without supervision thanks to a variational procedure. Experimental evaluations show that allowing such a conditioning translates into substantial improvements on downstream tasks.

it.title: Repomix: emبacchetta i repository per i modelli linguistici
it.summary: Repomix è uno strumento basato su TypeScript che raccoglie un intero repository di codice in un unico file ottimizzato per i modelli linguistici. Aiuta gli sviluppatori a nutrire i LLM con l'intera base di codice in modo efficiente.
it.why_it_matters: Facilita l'integrazione di repository complessi con i principali strumenti di intelligenza artificiale, semplificando il lavoro di analisi e sviluppo assistito.
it.extended_analysis:
Nel panorama dello sviluppo software assistito da IA, la gestione di codebase estese rappresenta spesso un collo di bottiglia. Repomix affronta questa sfida impacchettando l'intero progetto in un formato facilmente digeribile dai modelli linguistici.

Questo approccio consente di sfruttare strumenti avanzati come Claude, ChatGPT, DeepSeek e altri senza frammentare il contesto del codice sorgente.
it.context: Gli sviluppatori utilizzano sempre più spesso assistenti IA basati su LLM, ma la condivisione di intere strutture di progetto richiede formati compatibili e puliti.
key_takeaways: Converte un intero repository in un file ottimizzato per IA.
Compatibile con svariati LLM tra cui Claude, ChatGPT e DeepSeek.
Sviluppato in TypeScript con un elevato numero di stelle su GitHub.
highlights: Strumento open source per la preparazione di codebase.
Oltre 29.000 stelle su GitHub.

en.title: Repomix: Packing Codebases for AI Models
en.summary: Repomix is a TypeScript-based tool that packs an entire repository into a single, AI-friendly file. It is designed to help developers feed their codebases to large language models and other AI tools efficiently.
en.why_it_matters: It streamlines the process of providing complete project contexts to modern AI assistants, improving how developers analyze and build software.
en.extended_analysis:
As AI-driven development becomes standard, feeding large repositories into language models remains a challenge due to context fragmentation. Repomix solves this by consolidating code repositories into a unified file structure.

By supporting numerous AI platforms like Claude, ChatGPT, and DeepSeek, it bridges the gap between traditional codebases and modern machine learning interfaces.
en.context: Feeding complex code structures into LLMs usually requires manual splitting or custom scripts, highlighting the need for standardized packaging tools.
key_takeaways: Packs entire repositories into a single file for AI ingestion.
Works with major LLMs including Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini.
Written in TypeScript with strong community adoption on GitHub.
highlights: Single-file codebase packaging for AI tools.
Over 29,000 GitHub stars.

es.title: Repomix: Empaqueta repositorios para modelos de IA
es.summary: Repomix es una herramienta desarrollada en TypeScript que empaqueta un repositorio completo en un solo archivo optimizado para la inteligencia artificial. Facilita el suministro de bases de código a los modelos de lenguaje.
es.why_it_matters: Simplifica la integración de proyectos complejos con asistentes de IA, mejorando la eficiencia al trabajar con bases de código extensas.
es.extended_analysis:
El desarrollo asistido por IA requiere a menudo alimentar a los modelos con el contexto completo de un proyecto. Repomix aborda esta necesidad convirtiendo un repositorio entero en un formato claro y unificado.

La herramienta es compatible con múltiples plataformas de IA como Claude, ChatGPT, DeepSeek y Llama, facilitando flujos de trabajo avanzados.
es.context: La compartición de código fuente con modelos de lenguaje exige soluciones que eviten la pérdida de contexto en proyectos grandes.
key_takeaways: Convierte repositorios enteros en archivos aptos para IA.
Compatible con una amplia gama de LLM y herramientas de IA.
Desarrollado en TypeScript y muy popular en GitHub.
highlights: Agrupación de repositorios en un archivo único.
Más de 29.000 estrellas en GitHub.

zh-CN.title: Repomix：将代码库打包用于大语言模型
zh-CN.summary: Repomix 是一款基于 TypeScript 的工具，可将整个代码仓库打包成单个对人工智能友好的文件。它旨在帮助开发者高效地将代码库输入给大语言模型和其他 AI 工具。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 它简化了向现代 AI 助手提供完整项目上下文的过程，提升了代码分析与智能开发的效率。

在 AI 辅助开发的浪潮中，如何向大语言模型完整传递项目结构一直是一项挑战。Repomix 通过将整个代码库整合为单一文件来解决这一问题。

zh-CN.context: 将复杂的代码结构输入给 LLM 通常需要标准化的打包方案，以保持上下文的完整性。
key_takeaways: 将整个代码仓库打包为适合 AI 读取的单个文件。
兼容 Claude、ChatGPT、DeepSeek 等主流大模型。
采用 TypeScript 编写，在 GitHub 上备受关注。
highlights: 用于 AI 工具的代码库单文件打包方案。
在 GitHub 上获得超过 29,000 颗星。

de.title: Repomix: Codebasen für KI-Modelle verpacken
de.summary: Repomix ist ein TypeScript-basiertes Werkzeug, das ein vollständiges Repository in eine einzige, KI-freundliche Datei verpackt. Es hilft Entwicklern, ihre Codebasis effizient an Sprachmodelle zu übergeben.
de.why_it_matters: Es erleichtert die Bereitstellung kompletter Projektkontexte für moderne KI-Assistenten und optimiert die analyse- und entwicklungsbezogenen Abläufe.
de.extended_analysis:
Bei der KI-gestützten Softwareentwicklung ist die Handhabung großer Codebasen oft komplex. Repomix begegnet dieser Herausforderung, indem es das gesamte Repository in eine einheitliche Dateistruktur überführt.

Durch die Unterstützung verschiedener Sprachmodelle wie Claude, ChatGPT und DeepSeek schließt das Werkzeug die Lücke zwischen klassischen Projekten und KI-Schnittstellen.
de.context: Die Einspeisung umfangreicher Projektstrukturen in LLMs erfordert gut strukturierte Datenformate, um den Kontext zu bewahren.
key_takeaways: Verpackt komplette Repositories in eine einzelne KI-kompatible Datei.
Unterstützt gängige LLMs wie Claude, ChatGPT und Llama.
In TypeScript entwickelt mit starker GitHub-Community.
highlights: Einzeltausch-Verpackung für Codebasen und KI-Tools.
Über 29.000 GitHub-Sternchen.
